summary.text: Ancient history is the time period from the beginning of writing and recorded human history through late antiquity.
It covers all continents inhabited by humans from 3000 BC to AD 500, and the three-age system divides it into the Stone Age, the Bronze Age, and the Iron Age.
Over this time the world population kept climbing, from an estimated 45 million by 3000 BC to 209 million by AD 500.

facts.label: Recorded history
facts.value: Roughly 5,000 years, beginning with Sumerian cuneiform

facts.label: Göbekli Tepe
facts.value: Settlement began around 9500 BC; may have the oldest temple

facts.label: Writing's origins
facts.value: Developed separately in five different locations

items.prompt: A student says the Bronze Age began on the same date everywhere in the world. What is wrong with that claim?

options.label: The start and end of the ages vary between world regions
The ages were only ever defined for Europe
Every age began with the first use of writing
The Bronze Age is counted from the Iron Age's end

items.explain: The start and end of the three ages vary between world regions.

items.prompt: Between 10,000 BC and AD 500 the world population grew about a hundred times. What reason is given for the rapid rise?

options.label: The spread of iron weapons across the continents
The Neolithic Revolution, which was in full progress
The invention of writing in Mesopotamia
The migration of Homo sapiens out of Africa

items.explain: The world population was increasing exponentially during ancient history because of the Neolithic Revolution, which was in full progress.

items.prompt: A village keeps cattle, horses and donkeys for more than their meat. What extra thing do such animals do?

options.label: They lead herds of wild animals toward fresh water
They help hunters track other animals across hills
They carry and pull people and loads, greatly increasing human work
They help farmers store grain through the winter

items.explain: Domesticated animals were used not only for food but to carry and pull people and loads, greatly increasing human ability to do work.

items.prompt: Potters between 5000 and 4000 BC began shaping clay on a turning wheel. What did this invention later lead to for moving goods?

options.label: It became the simple plough used in fields
It led to the first pack animals being tamed
It allowed copper ores to first be smelted
It became wheeled vehicles that carry loads more easily

items.explain: By 3000 BC, the potter's wheel was adapted into wheeled vehicles that could carry loads further and more easily than people or animals alone.

items.prompt: A friend claims every writing system in the world descends from Sumerian cuneiform. What does the record say?

options.label: Writing developed separately in five different places
Writing spread outward from Mesopotamia to every region
Only Egypt and Mesopotamia ever developed writing
Writing arose independently in every inhabited region

items.explain: Writing developed separately in five different locations in human history: Mesopotamia, Egypt, India, China, and Mesoamerica.

items.prompt: Which region is treated as the cradle of civilisation, with some of the first law codes, empires and centralised governments?

options.label: Mesoamerica
The ancient Near East
New Guinea
Jomon Japan

items.explain: The ancient Near East is considered the cradle of civilisation, with the first centralised governments, law codes and empires.
